newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-GASOLINE DROP SEEN IN APIS, DEMAND EASING.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-GASOLINE DROP SEEN IN APIS, DEMAND EASING.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
UTILIZATION..... DN 0.50 PCT PT 97.1 DN 1.00 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected by dealers to report a gasoline stock decline Tuesday evening, but a drop in output is supposed to drive the decline as torrid demand begins to ease.
Gasoline stocks are expected to drop one to three million barrels as refinery utilization rates are seen easing 0.50 to one percentage point. The oil inventory data reflects the week ended August 8.

Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, are expected to show a seasonal one- to two-million barrel rise. Crude stocks, like gasoline stocks, are expected to decline by one to three million barrels.

"I would be in the camp that points to lower refinery runs. (Gasoline) Demand will still be good, maybe 8.3 million (barrels per day) or 8.1, but it won't be the same pace we have seen," said John Saucer, analyst with Smith Barney in Houston.

Implied gasoline demand has averaged around 8.6 million barrels a day (bpd) over the past three weeks to August 1. But, demand eased to 8.4 million bpd for the week ended August 1 from 8.8 million bpd the week before.

"We have some back-up of inventory on the secondary level (gasoline stations), so that prevents some movement from the primary (refinery) level," said Jim Ritterbusch, trader with with Sweeney Oil in Chicago.
Gasoline stocks have posted six consecutive weeks of declines as gasoline stations loaded up inventory to meet summer demand, but now inventory needs to be reduced on the retail level, dealers said.
Gasoline demand typically peaks in July and August, and retailers are wary of being stuck with inventory overhang as the summer enters its final weeks.
The API data reflects refiner inventory stock levels.

Meanwhile, crude stocks are seen dropping due to high refinery demand. The refinery utilization rate, although forecasted as easing, is still seen above a breakneck 95 percent. For the week ended August 1, it stood at 97.1 percent.
